data.why: the repo bundles examples/svk_k4.fa and examples/synthetic/* as ready-made alignments in every supported format, so the viewer's own example data is used directly via the ?url= query parameter and the in-app file-open dialog; nothing needs to be copied or synthesized.

goals: load a multiple sequence alignment (FASTA/Clustal/GenBank/BAM) and visually inspect conservation, gaps and subfamily structure
edit the alignment (residue edits, slide/move gaps, insert/delete columns) and realign a selected block with in-browser MAFFT
run codon-aware analysis to classify synonymous/non-synonymous changes and detect frameshifts in a coding alignment
cluster sequences into subfamilies by position-pattern and view diagnostic features
build a UPGMA or neighbour-joining tree from the alignment or a selection of rows
export the result as SVG, Word-compatible RTF, FASTA, or Newick for a figure or follow-up analysis

review.summary: The tree describes ViewAlign's purpose accurately: inspect, curate, analyse and export a multiple sequence alignment. Its phases, tasks and features sit at a sensible depth, and every screen I spot-checked supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: remove the codon step on the non-coding SINE data from t12, fold in the panel-only task, split undo history out of the block-realign feature, and add or flag the missing append-and-align and drag-editing work; the reads, annotation track and snapshot gaps are already noted in the tree.
